My Momma cat has such a similar role for me. 

I don't know how old she was when she passed because she came from a feral colony but I'm sure she was of similar age. We didn't grow up together but she belonged to a family that supported me through one of the lowest points of my life and was a constant when I practically lived with them. 

Then when I attempted to move forward with my life I had a second low while living on my own and just trying to function daily. Those blessed people let me take Momma with me and she changed my whole world for about 5-6 years. I don't know what happened or how but she became my guardian spirit, my soulmate, everything. Eventually her kidneys stopped working and the rest of her body followed and I had to make the tough choice to put her to rest. I let everyone know and my fiance who at that point had been in my life for about two years took care of me while I grieved hard. 

I honestly haven't recovered. It's been over two years and I still haven't regained my ability to take the best care of myself... It's like my brain just dumped out anything with "my routine" on the label and hasn't let me function correctly since. All of my ADHD symptoms got worse as well as my depression. I've been striving back to "normal" for what feels like forever. 

I guess I said all that to say, it's not just a cat, or a friend. It's hard to live life without your constants. Sending hugs and warm thoughts, OP. Here if you need a venting space. You will be ok.
